purpose: Compare bounded model-only, heuristic-only and model-plus-symbolic search under the original intuitionistic Peano kernel.
caveats: These cases were authored after inspecting existing training families and evaluation failures; they are exposed engineering diagnostics.
Absence of exact canonical statement hashes from the retained TRAIN and DEV rows does not exclude equivalent statements, template overlap, intermediate-state overlap or base-model exposure.
A bounded search failure is unknown, not a refutation. Negative-case truth labels come from separate reference refutations.
A Vampire success is only a solver proposal until the original constructive kernel accepts the complete proof.
Quantized local inference is not numerically identical to the archived GH200 evaluation.

cases.theorem: forall a b c d. a = b -> b = c -> c = d -> S (a + 5) = S (d + 5)
cases.purpose: Compose three equalities under a successor/addition context without induction.

cases.theorem: forall a b c. a = b -> c = b -> S (c + 6) = S (a + 6)
cases.purpose: Orient equalities and recognize an equivalent resulting state instead of looping on symmetry.

cases.theorem: forall a b c. (a = b /\ b = c) -> (c = a /\ S (a + 7) = S (c + 7))
cases.purpose: Unpack a hypothesis and preserve all remaining goals when splitting a target.

cases.theorem: forall a b c d. (a = b -> c = d) -> (c = d -> S (a + 8) = S (b + 8)) -> a = b -> S (a + 8) = S (b + 8)
cases.purpose: Use backward implication chaining; failed unrelated applications must not damage sibling states.

cases.theorem: forall a b. (forall z. z + 7 = 7 + z) -> S ((a + b) + 7) = S (7 + (a + b))
cases.purpose: Instantiate a universal premise at a composite term; commutativity is assumed here.

cases.theorem: forall n. exists w. w = S (n + 8) /\ S w = S (S (n + 8))
cases.purpose: Select a term already present in the goal and carry that witness into both conjuncts.

cases.theorem: forall a b. a = b -> (exists w. S w = a) -> exists w. S w = b
cases.purpose: Unpack an existential premise and reuse its witness after equality transport.

cases.theorem: forall a b. (S a = b \/ a = S b) -> (a = S b \/ S a = b)
cases.purpose: Split a disjunctive premise and choose different target sides for its two branches.

cases.theorem: forall a b c. (a = b \/ b = a) -> b = c -> (S a = S c \/ a + 9 = c + 9)
cases.purpose: Close both cases of a disjunction while orienting the same equality differently.
